_meta.indication: Indicated to reduce proteinuria in adults with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) at risk for disease progression; approved under accelerated approval based on reduction of proteinuria.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial; subjects randomized 1:1 to sibeprenlimab 400 mg SC Q4W or matching placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with biopsy-confirmed primary IgAN, eGFR ≥ 30 mL/min/1.73 m2, proteinuria (uPCR-24h ≥ 0.75 g/g or urine protein ≥ 1.0 g/day) on background ACEI and/or ARB therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: relative (percent) change from baseline in uPCR-24h at Month 9 (Week 40)
pivotal_trials.n: 530 randomized overall; interim analysis set N=320 (sibeprenlimab N=152, placebo N=168)
pivotal_trials.result: At Month 9, uPCR-24h reduced by 50.8% (96.5% CI: 42.4, 57.9) vs placebo; p<0.0001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were infections (49% vs 45% placebo) and injection site reactions (24% vs 23%); most common infection was upper respiratory infection (15% vs 14%) and most common injection site reaction was injection site erythema (13% vs 12%). Serious adverse events occurred in 3.5% of sibeprenlimab subjects vs 4.4% of placebo subjects.
target_moa: APRIL (A-Proliferation-Inducing Ligand) inhibitor; binds APRIL and blocks signaling at BCMA and TACI receptors, reducing levels of Gd-IgA1 implicated in IgAN pathogenesis.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; the application did not raise significant or controversial issues that would benefit from outside expertise or public discussion.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Reduction of proteinuria (substantial reduction in uPCR-24h at Month 9), accepted as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint for disease progression in IgAN.

citations.quote: Based on regulatory precedent and currently available data, the Division accepts a substantial reduction in proteinuria as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint for disease progression (loss of kidney function) in IgAN and as a basis for accelerated approval.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Required to conduct an adequate and well-controlled clinical trial to verify and describe clinical benefit (slowing kidney function decline long-term); to be addressed by completion of Trial 417-201-00007.

citations.quote: Pursuant to section 506(c) of the FDCA and 21 CFR 601.41, you are required to conduct an adequate and well-controlled clinical trial intended to verify and describe clinical benefit.
This requirement will be addressed by the completion of Trial 417-201-00007.

basis.text: Breakthrough therapy designation granted February 8, 2024 for the treatment of biopsy-confirmed IgAN.

citations.quote: On February 8, 2024, breakthrough therapy designation for the treatment of biopsy-confirmed IgAN was granted.

basis.text: Application was reviewed under Priority review.

summary.text: VOYXACT received breakthrough therapy designation (Feb 8, 2024) for biopsy-confirmed IgAN, was submitted as a priority-review BLA, and was granted accelerated approval based on reduction of proteinuria as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint, with a required confirmatory trial (417-201-00007) to verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: On February 8, 2024, breakthrough therapy designation for the treatment of biopsy-confirmed IgAN was granted.

Based on regulatory precedent and currently available data, the Division accepts a substantial reduction in proteinuria as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint for disease progression (loss of kidney function) in IgAN and as a basis for accelerated approval.
This requirement will be addressed by the completion of Trial 417-201-00007.

requirement.text: 4907-1: Conduct a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to describe and verify the clinical benefit of VOYXACT for primary IgA nephropathy (accelerated approval confirmatory trial).

citations.quote: 4907-1 Conduct a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to describe and verify the clinical benefit of Voyxart for the treatment of primary IgA nephropathy. The trial should be adequately powered and of sufficient duration to detect a treatment effect on the endpoint that will be used to describe and verify the clinical benefit.

requirement.text: 4907-2: Conduct a pharmacodynamic, pharmacokinetic, safety and tolerability study of VOYXACT in pediatric patients 2 to 17 years of age with primary IgAN (deferred PREA pediatric study).

citations.quote: 4907-2 Conduct a pharmacodynamic, pharmacokinetic, safety and tolerability study of Voyxact in pediatric patients 2 years to 17 years of age with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy. The pharmacodynamic assessment should be based on effects on proteinuria.

requirement.text: 4907-3: Perform a lactation study in lactating women who have received VOYXACT to measure concentrations of sibeprenlimab-szsi in breast milk.

citations.quote: 4907-3 Perform a lactation study (milk only or mother-infant pair study) in lactating women who have received Voyxact to measure concentrations of sibeprenlimab-szsi and its major metabolites in breast milk using a validated assay. Assess the effects on the breastfed infant, if available, based on study population.

requirement.text: 4907-4: Conduct a worldwide descriptive study collecting prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to VOYXACT during pregnancy to assess pregnancy/maternal complications and effects on the fetus, neonate, and infant.

citations.quote: 4907-4 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to Voyxact during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, and adverse effects on the developing fetus, neonate, and infant. Assess infant outcomes through at least the first year of life. The minimum number of patients will be specified in the protocol.
